title: Internationalization at home and global competence among Chinese university students: The mediating role of intercultural self-efficacy.
abstract: Internationalization at home (IaH) offers opportunities for intercultural learning without student mobility. Drawing on social cognitive theory and intergroup contact theory, this study examined indirect associations between perceived IaH and global competence through intercultural self-efficacy, alongside generalized self-efficacy. A two-wave survey of 435 Chinese university students measured IaH at T1 and both efficacy variables and competence at T2, approximately 4-6 weeks later. Self-developed measures were assessed using nonoverlapping development and confirmation subsamples. The primary item-level latent model treated knowledge, academic competence, international attitude, and values recognition as separate outcomes. IaH was positively associated with intercultural self-efficacy (β = 0.532). Its indirect associations through intercultural efficacy were positive for all four outcomes in the primary bootstrap analysis, whereas generalized-efficacy indirect associations were significant for three outcomes, excluding values recognition. Contrasts favored intercultural efficacy for knowledge and international attitude, but not conclusively for the other two outcomes. Explained variance ranged from 0.27 to 0.35. Inverse-probability weighting retained the knowledge, academic, and attitude indirect associations, while the values interval included zero. Including communication as a fifth latent outcome retained the four-outcome path pattern. Method-factor adjustment attenuated the IaH-efficacy associations. The findings support examining efficacy specificity and competence facets separately, with the values-recognition association requiring greater caution. Because efficacy and competence were measured concurrently, the indirect associations do not establish causal mediation.
